agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Install :cd: * macOS * [Homebrew](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/gping#default): `brew install gping` * [MacPorts](https://ports.macports.org/port/gping/): `sudo port install gping` * Linux (Homebrew): `brew install gping` * CentOS (and other distributions with an old glibc): Download the MUSL build from the latest release * Windows/ARM: * Scoop: `scoop install gping` * Chocolatey: `choco install gping` * Download the latest release from [the github releases page](https://github.com/orf/gping/releases) * Fedora ([COPR](https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/atim/gping/)): `sudo dnf copr enable atim/gping -y && sudo dnf install gping` * Cargo (**This requires `rustc` version 1.67.0 or greater**): `cargo install gping` * Arch Linux: `pacman -S gping` * Alpine linux: `apk add gping` * Ubuntu >23.10/Debian >13: `apt install gping` * Ubuntu/Debian ([Azlux's repo](https://packages.azlux.fr/)): ```bash echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/azlux.gpg] https://packages.azlux.fr/debian/ bookworm main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azlux.list sudo apt install gpg curl -s https://azlux.fr/repo.gpg.key | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/azlux.gpg > /dev/null sudo apt update sudo apt install gping ``` * Gentoo ([dm9pZCAq overlay](https://github.com/gentoo-mirror/dm9pZCAq)): ```sh sudo eselect repository enable dm9pZCAq sudo emerge --sync dm9pZCAq sudo emerge net-misc/gping::dm9pZCAq ``` * FreeBSD: * [pkg](https://www.freshports.org/net-mgmt/gping/): `pkg install gping` * [ports](https://cgit.freebsd.org/ports/tree/net-mgmt/gping) `cd /usr/ports/net-mgmt/gping; make install clean` * Docker: ```sh # Check all options docker run --rm -ti --network host ghcr.io/orf/gping:gping-v1.15.1 --help # Ping google.com docker run --rm -ti --network host ghcr.io/orf/gping:gping-v1.15.1 google.com ``` * Flox: ```sh # Inside of a Flox environment flox install gping ``` * [gah](https://github.com/marverix/gah): ```sh gah install gping ``` # Usage :saxophone: Just run `gping [host]`. `host` can be a command like `curl google.com` if the `--cmd` flag is used. You can also use shorthands like `aws:eu-west-1` or `aws:ca-central-1` to ping specific cloud regions. Only `aws` is currently supported. ```bash $ gping --help Ping, but with a graph. Usage: gping [OPTIONS] [HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS]... Arguments: [HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS]... Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if --cmd is provided. Can use cloud shorthands like aws:eu-west-1. Options: --cmd Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts -n, --watch-interval Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5'). Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5. -b, --buffer Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph. [default: 30] -4 Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address -6 Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address -i, --interface Interface to use when pinging -s, --simple-graphics Uses dot characters instead of braille --vertical-margin Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom) [default: 1] --horizontal-margin Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right) [default: 0] -c, --color Assign color to a graph entry. This option can be defined more than once as a comma separated string, and the order which the colors are provided will be matched against the hosts or commands passed to gping. Hexadecimal RGB color codes are accepted in the form of '#RRGGBB' or the following color names: 'black', 'red', 'green', 'yellow', 'blue', 'magenta','cyan', 'gray', 'dark-gray', 'light-red', 'light-green', 'light-yellow', 'light-blue', 'light-magenta', 'light-cyan', and 'white' -h, --help Print help information -V, --version Print version information --clear Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program ```

Inside of a Flox environment flox install gping ``` * [gah](https://github.com/marverix/gah): ```sh gah install gping ``` # Usage :saxophone: Just run `gping [host]`. `host` can be a command like `curl google.com` if the `--cmd` flag is used. # Very interesting! Multiple hosts share the same Y scale. 
# Headers are per-host, one per line at the top
# Now let me look at time formatting rules:
# - µs for microseconds when value < 1ms
# - ms for milliseconds when value >= 1ms
# - ns for nanoseconds when value < 1µs

# Let me look at what "jitter" is - likely the std deviation of recent pings
# Let me check "p95" - probably the 95th percentile
# And "t/o" - timeouts counter

# Now let me start writing the main application
# This is a complex TUI app. Let me look at what libraries are needed.

# The executable uses ratatui for TUI (tui-rs successor)
# Let me verify what version is needed
# key dependencies:
# - clap 4.x for CLI
# - ratatui for TUI
# - crossterm for terminal handling
# - chrono for timestamps

# Let me look at the bottom x-axis format:
# " 09:38:14                                             09:38:16.500                                        09:38:19"
# Times at start, middle, and end of graph
# Middle has .500 (sub-second precision)

# The format for p95 - it shows "0ns" when there's not enough data
# This is the 95th percentile ping time

# Let me check ratatui compatibility
cargo search ratatui 2>/dev/null | head -5 || true
# Let me check available versions
ls ~/.cargo/registry/cache/ 2>/dev/null | head -5 || echo "No cache"

# the width needed for the longest label.
# The chart widget occupies its full area including the y-axis.

# The header widget (Paragraph or similar) occupies its full area WITHOUT y-axis.
# In a layout with these two stacked vertically:
# [header] spans cols 0..W-1 (full width)
# [chart] spans cols 0..W-1 (full width)
# But internally, the chart renders y-axis at cols 0..(y_width-1), data at y_width..(W-1)

# The header has NO y-axis, so it spans the full W characters.
# But we measured header = 77 for W=80...
# THIS means the header does NOT span the full width!

# OR: maybe in ratatui, the chart is inside a Block/border, and the outer
# container is slightly smaller than terminal width?

# Let me look at this more carefully. When ratatui renders, there might be
# a Container block with no borders that just lays out vertically.
# Let me test with vertical-margin=0 to see if that changes anything.

tmux new-session -d -s testvm -x 80 -y 30
tmux send-keys -t testvm './executable --cmd "sleep 0.05" --buffer 3 --vertical-margin 0' Enter
sleep 3
tmux capture-pane -t testvm -p | head -5
tmux kill-session -t testvm

# For a line graph, we need to render the curve using braille characters

# bit 4 = dot5 (mid-right)

# The braille dot layout in ratatui canvas:

    print(f"{c} U+{code:04X} bits={bits:08b}")
EOF

def parse_color(color_str: str) -> str:

    if color_str in COLOR_NAMES:

    if re.match(r'^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$', color_str):
        return color_str
    raise ValueError(f"Invalid color code: `{color_str}`\n\nCaused by:\n    Failed to parse Colors")

def format_duration(nanos: int) -> str:
    """Format a duration in nanoseconds to human-readable string."""
    if nanos < 1000:
        return f"{nanos}ns"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000:
        return f"{nanos // 1000}µs"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000_000:
        ms = nanos / 1_000_000
        # Format with 3 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{ms:.3f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}ms"
    else:
        secs = nanos / 1_000_000_000
        # Format with 6 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{secs:.6f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}s"

def duration_to_nanos(seconds: float) -> int:
    """Convert seconds (float) to nanoseconds (int)."""
    return int(seconds * 1_000_000_000)

@dataclass
class PingData:
    """Data for a single host/command."""
    name: str
    display_name: str
    data: deque  # deque of (timestamp, nanos) or None for timeout
    timeout_count: int = 0
    lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock)
    
    def add_result(self, timestamp: float, nanos: Optional[int]):
        with self.lock:
            if nanos is None:
                self.timeout_count += 1
                self.data.append((timestamp, None))
            else:
                self.data.append((timestamp, nanos))
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            values = [v for _, v in self.data if v is not None]
            if not values:
                return {
                    'last': None,
                    'min': None,
                    'max': None,
                    'avg': None,
                    'jitter': 0,
                    'p95': 0,
                    'timeout': self.timeout_count
                }
            
            last = values[-1] if values else None
            mn = min(values)
            mx = max(values)
            avg = sum(values) / len(values)
            
            # Jitter: mean absolute consecutive difference
            if len(values) >= 2:
                diffs = [abs(values[i] - values[i-1]) for i in range(1, len(values))]
                jitter = sum(diffs) // len(diffs)
            else:
                jitter = 0
            
            # p95: 95th percentile
            sorted_v = sorted(values)
            p95_idx = int(len(sorted_v) * 0.95)
            if p95_idx >= len(sorted_v):
                p95_idx = len(sorted_v) - 1
            p95 = sorted_v[p95_idx] if sorted_v else 0
            
            return {
                'last': last,
                'min': mn,
                'max': mx,
                'avg': int(avg),
                'jitter': jitter,
                'p95': p95,
                'timeout': self.timeout_count
            }
    
    def get_data_for_display(self, start_time: float, end_time: float) -> list:
        """Get (timestamp, nanos) pairs for display window."""
        with self.lock:
            return [(t, v) for t, v in self.data if start_time <= t <= end_time]


def run_ping_command(host: str, ping_data: PingData, stop_event: threading.Event,
                     ipv4: bool, ipv6: bool, interface: Optional[str], 
                     watch_interval: float, extra_args: List[str]):
    """Run ping command in background thread."""
    # Build ping command
    if ipv6:
        cmd = ['ping6']
    else:
        cmd = ['ping']
    
    if ipv4 and not ipv6:
        cmd.append('-4')
    
    if interface:
        cmd.extend(['-I', interface])
    
    cmd.extend(extra_args)
    cmd.append(host)
    
    try:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                 text=True, bufsize=1)
        
        time_re = re.compile(r'time=(\d+(?:\.\d+)?) ms')
        timeout_re = re.compile(r'(?:Request timeout|no answer yet|Destination Host Unreachable)')
        
        for line in proc.stdout:
            if stop_event.is_set():
                break
            line = line.strip()
            m = time_re.search(line)
            if m:
                ms = float(m.group(1))
                nanos = int(ms * 1_000_000)
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
            elif timeout_re.search(line):
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: {e}")

                      watch_interval: float):
    """Run command repeatedly and measure execution time."""
    while not stop_event.is_set():
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(cmd_str, shell=True, 
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, 
                                    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            nanos = int(elapsed * 1_000_000_000)
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
        except Exception:
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        # Sleep for watch_interval (account for command execution time)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        sleep_time = max(0, watch_interval - elapsed)
        # But we already waited for command to finish, so just sleep watch_interval
        # Actually we want to sleep between runs, not interval including run time

# dot7(bit6) dot8(bit7)

BRAILLE_BASE = 0x2800
# For column 0 (left): bits 0,1,2,6 (dots 1,2,3,7) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
# For column 1 (right): bits 3,4,5,7 (dots 4,5,6,8) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
BRAILLE_LEFT = [0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x40]   # row 0,1,2,3 on left column
BRAILLE_RIGHT = [0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x80]  # row 0,1,2,3 on right column

def render_braille_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]], 
                          width: int, height: int,
                          y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[int]]:
    """
    Render multiple data sets as braille chart.
    
    Args:
        data_sets: list of [(x_frac, y_value)] where x_frac is 0..1
        width: chart width in chars
        height: chart height in chars (vertical)
        y_min, y_max: y-axis range
        
    Returns:
        grid[row][col] = bitmask for braille char
    """
    # Create grid: (height) rows x (width) cols
    # Each cell has a bitmask for braille dots
    grid = [[0] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    dot_height = height * 4  # total vertical dots
    dot_width = width * 2    # total horizontal dots
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            # Map x to dot column
            dot_x = int(x_frac * (dot_width - 1))
            dot_x = max(0, min(dot_width - 1, dot_x))
            
            # Map y to dot row (0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top)
            # Note: visual top = row 0 in grid (high values at top)
            dot_y_val = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            dot_y_val = max(0.0, min(1.0, dot_y_val))
            
            # dot_y in [0, dot_height-1] where 0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top
            dot_y = int(dot_y_val * (dot_height - 1))
            dot_y = max(0, min(dot_height - 1, dot_y))
            
            # Convert to char position
            char_col = dot_x // 2
            char_row = height - 1 - (dot_y // 4)  # invert: row 0 = top of display
            
            col_in_char = dot_x % 2  # 0 = left, 1 = right
            row_in_char = 3 - (dot_y % 4)  # invert: 0 = top dot, 3 = bottom dot
            
            if 0 <= char_row < height and 0 <= char_col < width:
                if col_in_char == 0:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_LEFT[row_in_char]
                else:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_RIGHT[row_in_char]

def render_dot_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]],
                     width: int, height: int,
                     y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[str]]:
    """
    Render as simple dot chart.
    
    Returns grid[row][col] = ' ' or '•'
    """
    grid = [[' '] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            x_col = int(x_frac * (width - 1))
            x_col = max(0, min(width - 1, x_col))
            
            y_norm = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            y_norm = max(0.0, min(1.0, y_norm))
            
            y_row = height - 1 - int(y_norm * (height - 1))
            y_row = max(0, min(height - 1, y_row))
            
            grid[y_row][x_col] = '•'
    
    return grid


def format_header_stats(stats: dict, col_width: int) -> str:
    """Format statistics for header display."""
    def fmt(val):
        if val is None:
            return "N/A"
        return format_duration(val)
    
    last = fmt(stats['last'])
    mn = fmt(stats['min'])
    mx = fmt(stats['max'])
    avg = fmt(int(stats['avg'])) if stats['avg'] is not None else "N/A"
    jtr = format_duration(stats['jitter'])
    p95 = format_duration(stats['p95'])
    
    fields = [
        f"last {last}",
        f"min {mn}",
        f"max {mx}",
        f"avg {avg}",
        f"jtr {jtr}",
        f"p95 {p95}",
    ]
    
    result = ""
    for f in fields:
        result += f"{f:<{col_width}}"
    result += f"t/o {stats['timeout']}"
    
    return result


def format_x_axis_time(t: float) -> str:
    """Format timestamp for x-axis label."""
    dt = time.localtime(t)
    ms = int((t % 1) * 1000)
    if ms == 0:
        return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", dt)
    else:
        return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", dt) + f".{ms:03d}"


def calculate_y_range(all_data: List[PingData], start_time: float, end_time: float):
    """Calculate min and max y values across all data sets."""
    all_values = []
    for pd in all_data:
        for _, v in pd.get_data_for_display(start_time, end_time):
            if v is not None:
                all_values.append(v)
    
    if not all_values:
        return 0, 1000000  # Default 0-1ms range
    
    return min(all_values), max(all_values)


def get_y_labels(y_min: float, y_max: float, n_labels: int) -> List[Tuple[float, str]]:
    """Generate y-axis labels."""
    labels = []
    for i in range(n_labels):
        val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / (n_labels - 1) if n_labels > 1 else y_min
        labels.append((val, format_duration(int(val))))

def resolve_host(host: str) -> str:
    """Resolve host name, handling cloud shortcuts."""
    if host.startswith('aws:'):
        region = host[4:]
        resolved = resolve_aws_host(region)
        # Try to resolve
        import socket
        try:
            socket.getaddrinfo(resolved, None)
        except socket.gaierror:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Resolving {resolved}\n\nCaused by:\n    failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known")
        return resolved
    return host

def format_duration(nanos: int) -> str:
    """Format a duration in nanoseconds to human-readable string."""
    if nanos < 1000:
        return f"{nanos}ns"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000:
        return f"{nanos // 1000}µs"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000_000:
        ms = nanos / 1_000_000
        # Format with 3 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{ms:.3f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}ms"
    else:

        # Format with 6 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{secs:.6f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}s"

def duration_to_nanos(seconds: float) -> int:

@dataclass
class PingData:
    """Data for a single host/command."""
    name: str
    display_name: str
    data: deque  # deque of (timestamp, nanos) or None for timeout
    timeout_count: int = 0
    lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock)
    
    def add_result(self, timestamp: float, nanos: Optional[int]):
        with self.lock:
            if nanos is None:
                self.timeout_count += 1
                self.data.append((timestamp, None))
            else:
                self.data.append((timestamp, nanos))
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            values = [v for _, v in self.data if v is not None]
            if not values:
                return {
                    'last': None,
                    'min': None,
                    'max': None,
                    'avg': None,
                    'jitter': 0,
                    'p95': 0,
                    'timeout': self.timeout_count
                }
            
            last = values[-1] if values else None
            mn = min(values)
            mx = max(values)
            avg = sum(values) / len(values)
            
            # Jitter: mean absolute consecutive difference
            if len(values) >= 2:
                diffs = [abs(values[i] - values[i-1]) for i in range(1, len(values))]
                jitter = sum(diffs) // len(diffs)
            else:
                jitter = 0
            
            # p95: 95th percentile
            sorted_v = sorted(values)
            p95_idx = int(len(sorted_v) * 0.95)
            if p95_idx >= len(sorted_v):
                p95_idx = len(sorted_v) - 1
            p95 = sorted_v[p95_idx] if sorted_v else 0
            
            return {
                'last': last,
                'min': mn,
                'max': mx,
                'avg': int(avg),
                'jitter': jitter,
                'p95': p95,
                'timeout': self.timeout_count
            }
    
    def get_data_for_display(self, start_time: float, end_time: float) -> list:
        """Get (timestamp, nanos) pairs for display window."""
        with self.lock:

    cmd.append(host)
    
    try:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                 text=True, bufsize=1)
        
        time_re = re.compile(r'time=(\d+(?:\.\d+)?) ms')
        timeout_re = re.compile(r'(?:Request timeout|no answer yet|Destination Host Unreachable)')
        
        for line in proc.stdout:
            if stop_event.is_set():
                break
            line = line.strip()
            m = time_re.search(line)
            if m:
                ms = float(m.group(1))
                nanos = int(ms * 1_000_000)
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
            elif timeout_re.search(line):
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: {e}")


def run_timed_command(cmd_str: str, ping_data: PingData, stop_event: threading.Event,
                      watch_interval: float):
    """Run command repeatedly and measure execution time."""
    while not stop_event.is_set():
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(cmd_str, shell=True, 
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, 
                                    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            nanos = int(elapsed * 1_000_000_000)
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
        except Exception:
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        # Sleep for watch_interval (account for command execution time)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        sleep_time = max(0, watch_interval - elapsed)
        # But we already waited for command to finish, so just sleep watch_interval
        # Actually we want to sleep between runs, not interval including run time
        # The actual gping sleeps watch_interval after each run
        time.sleep(watch_interval)


# Braille rendering
# Each braille char encodes a 2x4 dot grid
# bit layout (standard braille):
# dot1(bit0) dot4(bit3)
# dot2(bit1) dot5(bit4) 
# dot3(bit2) dot6(bit5)
# dot7(bit6) dot8(bit7)

BRAILLE_BASE = 0x2800
# For column 0 (left): bits 0,1,2,6 (dots 1,2,3,7) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
# For column 1 (right): bits 3,4,5,7 (dots 4,5,6,8) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
BRAILLE_LEFT = [0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x40]   # row 0,1,2,3 on left column
BRAILLE_RIGHT = [0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x80]  # row 0,1,2,3 on right column

def render_braille_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]], 
                          width: int, height: int,
                          y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[int]]:
    """
    Render multiple data sets as braille chart.
    
    Args:
        data_sets: list of [(x_frac, y_value)] where x_frac is 0..1
        width: chart width in chars
        height: chart height in chars (vertical)
        y_min, y_max: y-axis range
        
    Returns:
        grid[row][col] = bitmask for braille char
    """
    # Create grid: (height) rows x (width) cols
    # Each cell has a bitmask for braille dots
    grid = [[0] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    dot_height = height * 4  # total vertical dots
    dot_width = width * 2    # total horizontal dots
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            # Map x to dot column
            dot_x = int(x_frac * (dot_width - 1))
            dot_x = max(0, min(dot_width - 1, dot_x))
            
            # Map y to dot row (0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top)
            # Note: visual top = row 0 in grid (high values at top)
            dot_y_val = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            dot_y_val = max(0.0, min(1.0, dot_y_val))
            
            # dot_y in [0, dot_height-1] where 0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top
            dot_y = int(dot_y_val * (dot_height - 1))
            dot_y = max(0, min(dot_height - 1, dot_y))
            
            # Convert to char position
            char_col = dot_x // 2
            char_row = height - 1 - (dot_y // 4)  # invert: row 0 = top of display
            
            col_in_char = dot_x % 2  # 0 = left, 1 = right
            row_in_char = 3 - (dot_y % 4)  # invert: 0 = top dot, 3 = bottom dot
            
            if 0 <= char_row < height and 0 <= char_col < width:
                if col_in_char == 0:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_LEFT[row_in_char]
                else:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_RIGHT[row_in_char]
    
    return grid


def render_dot_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]],
                     width: int, height: int,
                     y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[str]]:
    """
    Render as simple dot chart.
    
    Returns grid[row][col] = ' ' or '•'
    """
    grid = [[' '] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            x_col = int(x_frac * (width - 1))
            x_col = max(0, min(width - 1, x_col))
            
            y_norm = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            y_norm = max(0.0, min(1.0, y_norm))
            
            y_row = height - 1 - int(y_norm * (height - 1))
            y_row = max(0, min(height - 1, y_row))
            
            grid[y_row][x_col] = '•'
    
    return grid


def format_header_stats(stats: dict, col_width: int) -> str:
    """Format statistics for header display."""
    def fmt(val):
        if val is None:
            return "N/A"
        return format_duration(val)
    
    last = fmt(stats['last'])
    mn = fmt(stats['min'])
    mx = fmt(stats['max'])
    avg = fmt(int(stats['avg'])) if stats['avg'] is not None else "N/A"
    jtr = format_duration(stats['jitter'])
    p95 = format_duration(stats['p95'])
    
    fields = [
        f"last {last}",
        f"min {mn}",
        f"max {mx}",
        f"avg {avg}",
        f"jtr {jtr}",
        f"p95 {p95}",
    ]
    
    result = ""
    for f in fields:
        result += f"{f:<{col_width}}"
    result += f"t/o {stats['timeout']}"
    
    return result


def format_x_axis_time(t: float) -> str:
    """Format timestamp for x-axis label."""
    dt = time.localtime(t)
    ms = int((t % 1) * 1000)
    if ms == 0:
        return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", dt)
    else:
        return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", dt) + f".{ms:03d}"


def calculate_y_range(all_data: List[PingData], start_time: float, end_time: float):
    """Calculate min and max y values across all data sets."""
    all_values = []
    for pd in all_data:
        for _, v in pd.get_data_for_display(start_time, end_time):
            if v is not None:
                all_values.append(v)
    
    if not all_values:
        return 0, 1000000  # Default 0-1ms range
    
    return min(all_values), max(all_values)


def get_y_labels(y_min: float, y_max: float, n_labels: int) -> List[Tuple[float, str]]:
    """Generate y-axis labels."""
    labels = []
    for i in range(n_labels):
        val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / (n_labels - 1) if n_labels > 1 else y_min
        labels.append((val, format_duration(int(val))))
    return labels


def gping_main(stdscr, args, ping_data_list):

def resolve_host(host: str) -> str:
    """Resolve host name, handling cloud shortcuts."""
    if host.startswith('aws:'):
        region = host[4:]
        resolved = resolve_aws_host(region)
        # Try to resolve
        import socket
        try:
            socket.getaddrinfo(resolved, None)
        except socket.gaierror:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Resolving {resolved}\n\nCaused by:\n    failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known")
        return resolved
    return host

    args = parser.parse_args()

def parse_color(color_str: str) -> str:
    """Parse a color string, returning a valid color name or hex."""
    color_str = color_str.strip()
    if color_str in COLOR_NAMES:
        return color_str
    if re.match(r'^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$', color_str):
        return color_str
    raise ValueError(f"Invalid color code: `{color_str}`\n\nCaused by:\n    Failed to parse Colors")

def format_duration(nanos: int) -> str:
    """Format a duration in nanoseconds to human-readable string."""
    if nanos < 1000:
        return f"{nanos}ns"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000:
        return f"{nanos // 1000}µs"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000_000:
        ms = nanos / 1_000_000
        # Format with 3 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{ms:.3f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}ms"
    else:
        secs = nanos / 1_000_000_000
        # Format with 6 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{secs:.6f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}s"

def duration_to_nanos(seconds: float) -> int:
    """Convert seconds (float) to nanoseconds (int)."""
    return int(seconds * 1_000_000_000)

@dataclass
class PingData:
    """Data for a single host/command."""
    name: str
    display_name: str
    data: deque  # deque of (timestamp, nanos) or None for timeout
    timeout_count: int = 0
    lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock)
    
    def add_result(self, timestamp: float, nanos: Optional[int]):
        with self.lock:
            if nanos is None:
                self.timeout_count += 1
                self.data.append((timestamp, None))
            else:
                self.data.append((timestamp, nanos))
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            values = [v for _, v in self.data if v is not None]
            if not values:
                return {
                    'last': None,
                    'min': None,
                    'max': None,
                    'avg': None,
                    'jitter': 0,
                    'p95': 0,
                    'timeout': self.timeout_count
                }
            
            last = values[-1] if values else None
            mn = min(values)
            mx = max(values)
            avg = sum(values) / len(values)
            
            # Jitter: mean absolute consecutive difference
            if len(values) >= 2:
                diffs = [abs(values[i] - values[i-1]) for i in range(1, len(values))]
                jitter = sum(diffs) // len(diffs)
            else:
                jitter = 0
            
            # p95: 95th percentile
            sorted_v = sorted(values)
            p95_idx = int(len(sorted_v) * 0.95)
            if p95_idx >= len(sorted_v):
                p95_idx = len(sorted_v) - 1
            p95 = sorted_v[p95_idx] if sorted_v else 0
            
            return {
                'last': last,
                'min': mn,
                'max': mx,
                'avg': int(avg),
                'jitter': jitter,
                'p95': p95,
                'timeout': self.timeout_count
            }
    
    def get_data_for_display(self, start_time: float, end_time: float) -> list:
        """Get (timestamp, nanos) pairs for display window."""
        with self.lock:
            return [(t, v) for t, v in self.data if start_time <= t <= end_time]


def run_ping_command(host: str, ping_data: PingData, stop_event: threading.Event,
                     ipv4: bool, ipv6: bool, interface: Optional[str], 
                     watch_interval: float, extra_args: List[str]):
    """Run ping command in background thread."""
    # Build ping command
    if ipv6:
        cmd = ['ping6']
    else:
        cmd = ['ping']
    
    if ipv4 and not ipv6:
        cmd.append('-4')
    
    if interface:
        cmd.extend(['-I', interface])
    
    cmd.extend(extra_args)
    cmd.append(host)
    
    try:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                 text=True, bufsize=1)
        
        time_re = re.compile(r'time=(\d+(?:\.\d+)?) ms')
        timeout_re = re.compile(r'(?:Request timeout|no answer yet|Destination Host Unreachable)')
        
        for line in proc.stdout:
            if stop_event.is_set():
                break
            line = line.strip()
            m = time_re.search(line)
            if m:
                ms = float(m.group(1))
                nanos = int(ms * 1_000_000)
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
            elif timeout_re.search(line):
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: {e}")


def run_timed_command(cmd_str: str, ping_data: PingData, stop_event: threading.Event,
                      watch_interval: float):
    """Run command repeatedly and measure execution time."""
    while not stop_event.is_set():
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(cmd_str, shell=True, 
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, 
                                    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            nanos = int(elapsed * 1_000_000_000)
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
        except Exception:
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        # Sleep for watch_interval (account for command execution time)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        sleep_time = max(0, watch_interval - elapsed)
        # But we already waited for command to finish, so just sleep watch_interval
        # Actually we want to sleep between runs, not interval including run time
        # The actual gping sleeps watch_interval after each run
        time.sleep(watch_interval)


# Braille rendering
# Each braille char encodes a 2x4 dot grid
# bit layout (standard braille):
# dot1(bit0) dot4(bit3)
# dot2(bit1) dot5(bit4) 
# dot3(bit2) dot6(bit5)
# dot7(bit6) dot8(bit7)

BRAILLE_BASE = 0x2800
# For column 0 (left): bits 0,1,2,6 (dots 1,2,3,7) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
# For column 1 (right): bits 3,4,5,7 (dots 4,5,6,8) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
BRAILLE_LEFT = [0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x40]   # row 0,1,2,3 on left column
BRAILLE_RIGHT = [0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x80]  # row 0,1,2,3 on right column

def render_braille_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]], 
                          width: int, height: int,
                          y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[int]]:
    """
    Render multiple data sets as braille chart.
    
    Args:
        data_sets: list of [(x_frac, y_value)] where x_frac is 0..1
        width: chart width in chars
        height: chart height in chars (vertical)
        y_min, y_max: y-axis range
        
    Returns:
        grid[row][col] = bitmask for braille char
    """
    # Create grid: (height) rows x (width) cols
    # Each cell has a bitmask for braille dots
    grid = [[0] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    dot_height = height * 4  # total vertical dots
    dot_width = width * 2    # total horizontal dots
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            # Map x to dot column
            dot_x = int(x_frac * (dot_width - 1))
            dot_x = max(0, min(dot_width - 1, dot_x))
            
            # Map y to dot row (0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top)
            # Note: visual top = row 0 in grid (high values at top)
            dot_y_val = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            dot_y_val = max(0.0, min(1.0, dot_y_val))
            
            # dot_y in [0, dot_height-1] where 0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top
            dot_y = int(dot_y_val * (dot_height - 1))
            dot_y = max(0, min(dot_height - 1, dot_y))
            
            # Convert to char position
            char_col = dot_x // 2
            char_row = height - 1 - (dot_y // 4)  # invert: row 0 = top of display
            
            col_in_char = dot_x % 2  # 0 = left, 1 = right
            row_in_char = 3 - (dot_y % 4)  # invert: 0 = top dot, 3 = bottom dot
            
            if 0 <= char_row < height and 0 <= char_col < width:
                if col_in_char == 0:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_LEFT[row_in_char]
                else:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_RIGHT[row_in_char]
    
    return grid


def render_dot_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]],
                     width: int, height: int,
                     y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[str]]:
    """
    Render as simple dot chart.
    
    Returns grid[row][col] = ' ' or '•'
    """
    grid = [[' '] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            x_col = int(x_frac * (width - 1))
            x_col = max(0, min(width - 1, x_col))
            
            y_norm = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            y_norm = max(0.0, min(1.0, y_norm))
            
            y_row = height - 1 - int(y_norm * (height - 1))
            y_row = max(0, min(height - 1, y_row))
            
            grid[y_row][x_col] = '•'
    
    return grid


def format_header_stats(stats: dict, col_width: int) -> str:
    """Format statistics for header display."""
    def fmt(val):
        if val is None:
            return "N/A"
        return format_duration(val)
    
    last = fmt(stats['last'])
    mn = fmt(stats['min'])
    mx = fmt(stats['max'])
    avg = fmt(int(stats['avg'])) if stats['avg'] is not None else "N/A"
    jtr = format_duration(stats['jitter'])
    p95 = format_duration(stats['p95'])
    
    fields = [
        f"last {last}",
        f"min {mn}",
        f"max {mx}",
        f"avg {avg}",
        f"jtr {jtr}",
        f"p95 {p95}",
    ]
    
    result = ""
    for f in fields:
        result += f"{f:<{col_width}}"
    result += f"t/o {stats['timeout']}"
    
    return result


def format_x_axis_time(t: float) -> str:
    """Format timestamp for x-axis label."""
    dt = time.localtime(t)
    ms = int((t % 1) * 1000)
    if ms == 0:
        return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", dt)
    else:
        return time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", dt) + f".{ms:03d}"


def calculate_y_range(all_data: List[PingData], start_time: float, end_time: float):
    """Calculate min and max y values across all data sets."""
    all_values = []
    for pd in all_data:
        for _, v in pd.get_data_for_display(start_time, end_time):
            if v is not None:
                all_values.append(v)
    
    if not all_values:
        return 0, 1000000  # Default 0-1ms range
    
    return min(all_values), max(all_values)


def get_y_labels(y_min: float, y_max: float, n_labels: int) -> List[Tuple[float, str]]:
    """Generate y-axis labels."""
    labels = []
    for i in range(n_labels):
        val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / (n_labels - 1) if n_labels > 1 else y_min
        labels.append((val, format_duration(int(val))))
    return labels


def gping_main(stdscr, args, ping_data_list):
    """Main gping TUI function."""
    curses.curs_set(0)
    stdscr.nodelay(True)
    stdscr.timeout(100)
    
    # Initialize colors
    curses.start_color()
    curses.use_default_colors()
    
    # Color pairs: 1=green, 2=blue, 3=red, 4=yellow, 5=magenta, 6=cyan, 7=white
    color_pairs = {}
    default_color_list = ['green', 'blue', 'red', 'yellow', 'magenta', 'cyan', 'white']
    
    def get_color_pair(color_name: str, idx: int) -> int:
        if color_name not in color_pairs:
            pair_id = idx + 1
            if color_name.startswith('#'):
                # Hex color - try to use it as RGB if terminal supports
                r = int(color_name[1:3], 16)
                g = int(color_name[3:5], 16)
                b = int(color_name[5:7], 16)
                # curses color indices 16+ for custom colors
                color_idx = 16 + idx
                try:
                    curses.init_color(color_idx, r * 1000 // 255, g * 1000 // 255, b * 1000 // 255)
                    curses.init_pair(pair_id, color_idx, -1)
                except:
                    curses.init_pair(pair_id, curses.COLOR_WHITE, -1)
            else:
                curses_color = COLOR_NAMES.get(color_name, curses.COLOR_WHITE)
                curses.init_pair(pair_id, curses_color, -1)
            color_pairs[color_name] = pair_id
        return color_pairs[color_name]
    
    # Set up colors for each host
    host_colors = []
    for i, pd in enumerate(ping_data_list):
        if args.color and i < len(args.color):
            color = args.color[i]
        else:
            color = default_color_list[i % len(default_color_list)]
        host_colors.append(color)
    
    # Initialize color pairs
    for i, color in enumerate(host_colors):
        get_color_pair(color, i)
    
    buffer_secs = args.buffer
    v_margin = args.vertical_margin
    h_margin = args.horizontal_margin
    
    while True:
        # Handle input
        key = stdscr.getch()
        if key == ord('q') or key == 27:  # q or ESC
            break
        
        # Get terminal size
        height, width = stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        # Calculate layout
        n_hosts = len(ping_data_list)
        header_height = n_hosts  # One line per host
        
        # Available chart height (minus header, margins, x-axis)
        chart_height = height - header_height - v_margin * 2 - 2  # 2 for x-axis
        if chart_height < 3:
            chart_height = 3
        
        chart_width = width - h_margin * 2
        
        # Calculate current time window
        now = time.time()
        end_time = now
        start_time = now - buffer_secs
        
        # Get all values for y-range
        y_min, y_max = calculate_y_range(ping_data_list, start_time, end_time)
        
        if y_max <= y_min:
            y_max = y_min + 1
        
        # Add some padding to y range
        y_range = y_max - y_min
        if y_range == 0:
            y_range = y_max * 0.1 if y_max > 0 else 1000000
        
        # Number of y-axis labels
        n_y_labels = (chart_height + 7) // 8 + 1  # approximately every 8 rows
        
        # Calculate y-axis label width
        y_labels = []
        for i in range(n_y_labels):
            val = y_min + y_range * i / (n_y_labels - 1) if n_y_labels > 1 else y_min
            label = format_duration(int(val))
            y_labels.append((val, label))
        
        max_label_width = max(len(l) for _, l in y_labels) if y_labels else 6
        y_axis_width = max_label_width + 1  # +1 for │
        
        # Actual chart data area width
        data_width = chart_width - y_axis_width
        if data_width < 10:
            data_width = 10
        
        # Stat column width
        stat_col_width = width // 10
        name_col_width = stat_col_width * 3
        
        # Clear screen
        stdscr.erase()
        
        # Draw vertical margin
        for _ in range(v_margin):
            pass  # Just skip rows
        
        # Draw header rows
        for host_idx, pd in enumerate(ping_data_list):
            stats = pd.get_stats()
            
            y_pos = v_margin + host_idx
            if y_pos >= height:
                break
            
            # Format header line
            name_part = pd.display_name[:name_col_width]
            name_part = f"{name_part:<{name_col_width}}"
            
            stats_part = format_header_stats(stats, stat_col_width)
            
            line = (h_margin * ' ') + name_part + stats_part
            
            color_pair = get_color_pair(host_colors[host_idx], host_idx)
            
            # Draw name
            x_pos = h_margin
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(y_pos, x_pos, name_part, curses.color_pair(color_pair) | curses.A_BOLD)
                stdscr.addstr(y_pos, x_pos + name_col_width, stats_part)
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Draw chart
        chart_top = v_margin + header_height
        
        # Calculate y-axis labels for chart rows
        n_y_labels_chart = (chart_height // 8) + 2
        
        # Get data for display
        display_data = []
        for pd in ping_data_list:
            data = pd.get_data_for_display(start_time, end_time)
            # Convert to (x_frac, y_val) pairs
            if data:
                points = []
                for t, v in data:
                    x_frac = (t - start_time) / buffer_secs
                    points.append((x_frac, v))
                display_data.append(points)
            else:
                display_data.append([])
        
        # Render chart
        if args.simple_graphics:
            grid = render_dot_chart(display_data, data_width, chart_height, y_min, y_max)
        else:
            grid_braille = render_braille_chart(display_data, data_width, chart_height, y_min, y_max)
            # Convert braille bitmasks to chars
            grid = [[chr(BRAILLE_BASE + cell) if cell != 0 else ' ' 
                     for cell in row] for row in grid_braille]
        
        # Calculate y-axis label positions
        y_label_positions = {}
        for i in range(chart_height):
            # What value does this row represent?
            # Row 0 = top of chart = y_max
            # Row chart_height-1 = bottom = y_min
            row_val = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * i / (chart_height - 1) if chart_height > 1 else y_max
            y_label_positions[i] = row_val
        
        # Calculate which rows get y-axis labels
        y_axis_rows = {}
        # Determine evenly spaced label rows
        label_step = max(1, chart_height // (n_y_labels_chart - 1)) if n_y_labels_chart > 1 else chart_height
        labeled_rows = list(range(0, chart_height, label_step))
        if labeled_rows and labeled_rows[-1] != chart_height - 1:
            labeled_rows.append(chart_height - 1)
        
        for row in labeled_rows:
            val = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * row / (chart_height - 1) if chart_height > 1 else y_max
            y_axis_rows[row] = format_duration(int(val))
        
        # Draw chart rows
        for row in range(chart_height):
            y_pos = chart_top + row
            if y_pos >= height - 2:
                break
            
            x_pos = h_margin
            
            # Y-axis label
            if row in y_axis_rows:
                label = y_axis_rows[row]
                label_str = f"{label:>{max_label_width}}"
            else:
                label_str = ' ' * max_label_width
            
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(y_pos, x_pos, label_str)
                stdscr.addstr(y_pos, x_pos + max_label_width, '│')
            except curses.error:
                pass
            
            # Chart data
            chart_x_start = x_pos + y_axis_width
            
            if args.simple_graphics:
                row_str = ''.join(grid[row])
            else:
                row_str = ''.join(grid[row])
            
            # Draw the row data with colors
            # For simplicity, draw all data in combined form first
            # TODO: Handle per-host colors properly
            for col, ch in enumerate(row_str):
                if ch != ' ':
                    # Determine which host owns this dot
                    # For braille, multiple hosts may share a char
                    # For simplicity, use first host's color for non-empty chars
                    cx = chart_x_start + col
                    if cx < width:
                        try:
                            stdscr.addstr(y_pos, cx, ch, curses.color_pair(1))
                        except curses.error:
                            pass
        
        # Draw bottom border (x-axis)
        border_row = chart_top + chart_height
        if border_row < height - 1:
            x_pos = h_margin
            border_label = ' ' * max_label_width + '└' + '─' * data_width
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(border_row, x_pos, border_label[:width-x_pos])
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Draw x-axis timestamps
        ts_row = border_row + 1
        if ts_row < height:
            t_start_str = ' ' + format_x_axis_time(start_time)
            t_mid = start_time + buffer_secs / 2
            t_mid_str = format_x_axis_time(t_mid)
            t_end_str = format_x_axis_time(end_time)
            
            x_pos = h_margin + y_axis_width
            
            # Position start time
            ts_line = [' '] * data_width
            
            # Start label (left-aligned with offset 1)
            for i, ch in enumerate(t_start_str):
                if i < len(ts_line):
                    ts_line[i] = ch
            
            # Middle label (centered)
            mid_pos = data_width // 2 - len(t_mid_str) // 2
            for i, ch in enumerate(t_mid_str):
                pos = mid_pos + i
                if 0 <= pos < len(ts_line):
                    ts_line[pos] = ch
            
            # End label (right-aligned)
            end_pos = data_width - len(t_end_str)
            for i, ch in enumerate(t_end_str):
                pos = end_pos + i
                if 0 <= pos < len(ts_line):
                    ts_line[pos] = ch
            
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(ts_row, x_pos - y_axis_width, ''.join(ts_line[:width - (x_pos - y_axis_width)]))
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        stdscr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.1)


def resolve_host(host: str) -> str:
    """Resolve host name, handling cloud shortcuts."""
    if host.startswith('aws:'):
        region = host[4:]
        resolved = resolve_aws_host(region)
        # Try to resolve
        import socket
        try:
            socket.getaddrinfo(resolved, None)
        except socket.gaierror:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Resolving {resolved}\n\nCaused by:\n    failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known")
        return resolved
    return host


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog='gping',
        description='Ping, but with a graph.',
        add_help=False
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('hosts_or_commands', nargs='*', 
                        metavar='HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS',
                        help='Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if --cmd is provided. '
                             'Can use cloud shorthands like aws:eu-west-1')
    parser.add_argument('--cmd', action='store_true',
                        help='Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts')
    parser.add_argument('-n', '--watch-interval', type=float, metavar='WATCH_INTERVAL',
                        help="Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5'). "
                             "Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5")
    parser.add_argument('-b', '--buffer', type=int, default=30, metavar='BUFFER',
                        help='Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph [default: 30]')
    parser.add_argument('-4', dest='ipv4', action='store_true',
                        help='Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address')
    parser.add_argument('-6', dest='ipv6', action='store_true',
                        help='Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address')
    parser.add_argument('-i', '--interface', metavar='INTERFACE',
                        help='Interface to use when pinging')

"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

# AWS region to hostname mapping

COLOR_NAMES = {

}

def parse_color(color_str: str) -> str:
    """Parse a color string, returning a valid color name or hex."""
    color_str = color_str.strip()
    if color_str in COLOR_NAMES:
        return color_str
    if re.match(r'^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$', color_str):
        return color_str
    raise ValueError(f"Invalid color code: `{color_str}`\n\nCaused by:\n    Failed to parse Colors")

def format_duration(nanos: int) -> str:
    """Format a duration in nanoseconds to human-readable string."""
    if nanos < 1000:
        return f"{nanos}ns"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000:
        return f"{nanos // 1000}µs"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000_000:
        ms = nanos / 1_000_000
        # Format with 3 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{ms:.3f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}ms"
    else:
        secs = nanos / 1_000_000_000
        # Format with 6 decimal places, strip trailing zeros
        s = f"{secs:.6f}"
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
        return f"{s}s"

def duration_to_nanos(seconds: float) -> int:
    """Convert seconds (float) to nanoseconds (int)."""
    return int(seconds * 1_000_000_000)

@dataclass
class PingData:
    """Data for a single host/command."""
    name: str
    display_name: str
    data: deque  # deque of (timestamp, nanos) or None for timeout
    timeout_count: int = 0
    lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock)
    
    def add_result(self, timestamp: float, nanos: Optional[int]):
        with self.lock:
            if nanos is None:
                self.timeout_count += 1
                self.data.append((timestamp, None))
            else:
                self.data.append((timestamp, nanos))
    
    def get_stats(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            values = [v for _, v in self.data if v is not None]
            if not values:
                return {
                    'last': None,
                    'min': None,
                    'max': None,
                    'avg': None,
                    'jitter': 0,
                    'p95': 0,
                    'timeout': self.timeout_count
                }
            
            last = values[-1] if values else None
            mn = min(values)
            mx = max(values)
            avg = sum(values) / len(values)
            
            # Jitter: mean absolute consecutive difference
            if len(values) >= 2:
                diffs = [abs(values[i] - values[i-1]) for i in range(1, len(values))]
                jitter = sum(diffs) // len(diffs)
            else:
                jitter = 0
            
            # p95: 95th percentile
            sorted_v = sorted(values)
            p95_idx = int(len(sorted_v) * 0.95)
            if p95_idx >= len(sorted_v):
                p95_idx = len(sorted_v) - 1
            p95 = sorted_v[p95_idx] if sorted_v else 0
            
            return {
                'last': last,
                'min': mn,
                'max': mx,
                'avg': int(avg),
                'jitter': jitter,
                'p95': p95,
                'timeout': self.timeout_count
            }
    
    def get_data_for_display(self, start_time: float, end_time: float) -> list:
        """Get (timestamp, nanos) pairs for display window."""
        with self.lock:
            return [(t, v) for t, v in self.data if start_time <= t <= end_time]


def run_ping_command(host: str, ping_data: PingData, stop_event: threading.Event,
                     ipv4: bool, ipv6: bool, interface: Optional[str], 
                     watch_interval: float, extra_args: List[str]):
    """Run ping command in background thread."""
    # Build ping command
    if ipv6:
        cmd = ['ping6']
    else:
        cmd = ['ping']
    
    if ipv4 and not ipv6:
        cmd.append('-4')
    
    if interface:
        cmd.extend(['-I', interface])
    
    cmd.extend(extra_args)
    cmd.append(host)
    
    try:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                 text=True, bufsize=1)
        
        time_re = re.compile(r'time=(\d+(?:\.\d+)?) ms')
        timeout_re = re.compile(r'(?:Request timeout|no answer yet|Destination Host Unreachable)')
        
        for line in proc.stdout:
            if stop_event.is_set():
                break
            line = line.strip()
            m = time_re.search(line)
            if m:
                ms = float(m.group(1))
                nanos = int(ms * 1_000_000)
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
            elif timeout_re.search(line):
                ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Error spawning ping: {e}")


def run_timed_command(cmd_str: str, ping_data: PingData, stop_event: threading.Event,
                      watch_interval: float):
    """Run command repeatedly and measure execution time."""
    while not stop_event.is_set():
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(cmd_str, shell=True, 
                                    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, 
                                    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            nanos = int(elapsed * 1_000_000_000)
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), nanos)
        except Exception:
            ping_data.add_result(time.time(), None)
        
        # Sleep for watch_interval (account for command execution time)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        sleep_time = max(0, watch_interval - elapsed)
        # But we already waited for command to finish, so just sleep watch_interval
        # Actually we want to sleep between runs, not interval including run time
        # The actual gping sleeps watch_interval after each run
        time.sleep(watch_interval)


# Braille rendering
# Each braille char encodes a 2x4 dot grid
# bit layout (standard braille):
# dot1(bit0) dot4(bit3)
# dot2(bit1) dot5(bit4) 
# dot3(bit2) dot6(bit5)
# dot7(bit6) dot8(bit7)

BRAILLE_BASE = 0x2800
# For column 0 (left): bits 0,1,2,6 (dots 1,2,3,7) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
# For column 1 (right): bits 3,4,5,7 (dots 4,5,6,8) -> rows 0,1,2,3 from top
BRAILLE_LEFT = [0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x40]   # row 0,1,2,3 on left column
BRAILLE_RIGHT = [0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x80]  # row 0,1,2,3 on right column

def render_braille_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]], 
                          width: int, height: int,
                          y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[int]]:
    """
    Render multiple data sets as braille chart.
    
    Args:
        data_sets: list of [(x_frac, y_value)] where x_frac is 0..1
        width: chart width in chars
        height: chart height in chars (vertical)
        y_min, y_max: y-axis range
        
    Returns:
        grid[row][col] = bitmask for braille char
    """
    # Create grid: (height) rows x (width) cols
    # Each cell has a bitmask for braille dots
    grid = [[0] * width for _ in range(height)]
    
    dot_height = height * 4  # total vertical dots
    dot_width = width * 2    # total horizontal dots
    
    if y_max <= y_min:
        y_max = y_min + 1
    
    y_range = y_max - y_min
    
    for dataset in data_sets:
        for x_frac, y_val in dataset:
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            
            # Map x to dot column
            dot_x = int(x_frac * (dot_width - 1))
            dot_x = max(0, min(dot_width - 1, dot_x))
            
            # Map y to dot row (0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top)
            # Note: visual top = row 0 in grid (high values at top)
            dot_y_val = (y_val - y_min) / y_range
            dot_y_val = max(0.0, min(1.0, dot_y_val))
            
            # dot_y in [0, dot_height-1] where 0 = bottom, dot_height-1 = top
            dot_y = int(dot_y_val * (dot_height - 1))
            dot_y = max(0, min(dot_height - 1, dot_y))
            
            # Convert to char position
            char_col = dot_x // 2
            char_row = height - 1 - (dot_y // 4)  # invert: row 0 = top of display
            
            col_in_char = dot_x % 2  # 0 = left, 1 = right
            row_in_char = 3 - (dot_y % 4)  # invert: 0 = top dot, 3 = bottom dot
            
            if 0 <= char_row < height and 0 <= char_col < width:
                if col_in_char == 0:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_LEFT[row_in_char]
                else:
                    grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_RIGHT[row_in_char]
    
    return grid


def render_dot_chart(data_sets: List[List[Tuple[float, float]]],
                     width: int, height: int,
                     y_min: float, y_max: float) -> List[List[str]]:
    """

            y_row = max(0, min(height - 1, y_row))

            val = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * row / (chart_height - 1) if chart_height > 1 else y_max
            y_axis_rows[row] = format_duration(int(val))
        
        # Draw chart rows
        for row in range(chart_height):
            y_pos = chart_top + row
            if y_pos >= height - 2:
                break
            
            x_pos = h_margin
            
            # Y-axis label
            if row in y_axis_rows:
                label = y_axis_rows[row]
                label_str = f"{label:>{max_label_width}}"
            else:
                label_str = ' ' * max_label_width
            
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(y_pos, x_pos, label_str)
                stdscr.addstr(y_pos, x_pos + max_label_width, '│')
            except curses.error:
                pass
            
            # Chart data
            chart_x_start = x_pos + y_axis_width
            
            if args.simple_graphics:
                row_str = ''.join(grid[row])
            else:
                row_str = ''.join(grid[row])
            
            # Draw the row data with colors
            # For simplicity, draw all data in combined form first
            # TODO: Handle per-host colors properly
            for col, ch in enumerate(row_str):
                if ch != ' ':
                    # Determine which host owns this dot
                    # For braille, multiple hosts may share a char
                    # For simplicity, use first host's color for non-empty chars
                    cx = chart_x_start + col
                    if cx < width:
                        try:
                            stdscr.addstr(y_pos, cx, ch, curses.color_pair(1))
                        except curses.error:
                            pass
        
        # Draw bottom border (x-axis)
        border_row = chart_top + chart_height
        if border_row < height - 1:
            x_pos = h_margin
            border_label = ' ' * max_label_width + '└' + '─' * data_width
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(border_row, x_pos, border_label[:width-x_pos])
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Draw x-axis timestamps
        ts_row = border_row + 1
        if ts_row < height:
            t_start_str = ' ' + format_x_axis_time(start_time)
            t_mid = start_time + buffer_secs / 2
            t_mid_str = format_x_axis_time(t_mid)
            t_end_str = format_x_axis_time(end_time)
            
            x_pos = h_margin + y_axis_width
            
            # Position start time
            ts_line = [' '] * data_width
            
            # Start label (left-aligned with offset 1)
            for i, ch in enumerate(t_start_str):
                if i < len(ts_line):
                    ts_line[i] = ch
            
            # Middle label (centered)
            mid_pos = data_width // 2 - len(t_mid_str) // 2
            for i, ch in enumerate(t_mid_str):
                pos = mid_pos + i
                if 0 <= pos < len(ts_line):
                    ts_line[pos] = ch
            
            # End label (right-aligned)
            end_pos = data_width - len(t_end_str)
            for i, ch in enumerate(t_end_str):
                pos = end_pos + i
                if 0 <= pos < len(ts_line):
                    ts_line[pos] = ch
            
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(ts_row, x_pos - y_axis_width, ''.join(ts_line[:width - (x_pos - y_axis_width)]))
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        stdscr.refresh()
        time.sleep(0.1)


def resolve_host(host: str) -> str:
    """Resolve host name, handling cloud shortcuts."""
    if host.startswith('aws:'):
        region = host[4:]
        resolved = resolve_aws_host(region)
        # Try to resolve
        import socket
        try:
            socket.getaddrinfo(resolved, None)
        except socket.gaierror:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Resolving {resolved}\n\nCaused by:\n    failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known")
        return resolved
    return host


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog='gping',
        description='Ping, but with a graph.',
        add_help=False
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('hosts_or_commands', nargs='*', 
                        metavar='HOSTS_OR_COMMANDS',
                        help='Hosts or IPs to ping, or commands to run if --cmd is provided. '
                             'Can use cloud shorthands like aws:eu-west-1')
    parser.add_argument('--cmd', action='store_true',
                        help='Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts')
    parser.add_argument('-n', '--watch-interval', type=float, metavar='WATCH_INTERVAL',
                        help="Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5'). "
                             "Default for ping is 0.2, default for cmd is 0.5")
    parser.add_argument('-b', '--buffer', type=int, default=30, metavar='BUFFER',
                        help='Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph [default: 30]')
    parser.add_argument('-4', dest='ipv4', action='store_true',
                        help='Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address')
    parser.add_argument('-6', dest='ipv6', action='store_true',
                        help='Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address')
    parser.add_argument('-i', '--interface', metavar='INTERFACE',
                        help='Interface to use when pinging')
    parser.add_argument('-s', '--simple-graphics', action='store_true',
                        help='Uses dot characters instead of braille')
    parser.add_argument('--vertical-margin', type=int, default=1, metavar='VERTICAL_MARGIN',
                        help='Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom) [default: 1]')
    parser.add_argument('--horizontal-margin', type=int, default=0, metavar='HORIZONTAL_MARGIN',
                        help='Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right) [default: 0]')
    parser.add_argument('-c', '--color', action='append', metavar='color',
                        help='Assign color to a graph entry.')
    parser.add_argument('--clear', action='store_true',
                        help='Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program')
    parser.add_argument('--ping-args', nargs='*', metavar='PING_ARGS',
                        help="Extra arguments to pass to `ping`. These are platform dependent")
    parser.add_argument('-h', '--help', action='store_true',
                        help='Print help')
    parser.add_argument('-V', '--version', action='store_true',
                        help='Print version')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.help:
        parser.print_help()
        sys.exit(0)
    
    if args.version:
        print(f"gping {VERSION}")
        print(f"commit_hash: {COMMIT_HASH}")
        print(f"build_time: {BUILD_TIME}")
        print(f"build_env: {BUILD_ENV}")
        sys.exit(0)
    
    # Process color arguments
    colors = []
    if args.color:
        for c_str in args.color:
            for c in c_str.split(','):
                c = c.strip()
                try:
                    colors.append(parse_color(c))
                except ValueError as e:
                    print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                    sys.exit(1)
    args.color = colors if colors else None
    
    if not args.hosts_or_commands:
        print("Error: At least one host or command must be given (i.e gping google.com). "
              "Use --help for a full list of arguments.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Set default watch interval
    if args.watch_interval is None:
        args.watch_interval = 0.5 if args.cmd else 0.2
    
    # Resolve hosts and create ping data structures
    ping_data_list = []
    
    buffer_samples = int(args.buffer / args.watch_interval) + 10
    
    for host in args.hosts_or_commands:
        if args.cmd:
            display_name = host
        else:
            try:
                resolved = resolve_host(host)
                display_name = host
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(1)
        
        pd = PingData(
            name=host,
            display_name=display_name,
            data=deque(maxlen=buffer_samples)
        )
        ping_data_list.append(pd)
    
    # Start background threads
    stop_event = threading.Event()
    threads = []
    
    extra_args = args.ping_args or []
    
    for i, (host, pd) in enumerate(zip(args.hosts_or_commands, ping_data_list)):
        if args.cmd:
            t = threading.Thread(
                target=run_timed_command,
                args=(host, pd, stop_event, args.watch_interval),
                daemon=True
            )
        else:
            try:
                resolved = resolve_host(host)
            except RuntimeError as e:
                print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                stop_event.set()
                sys.exit(1)
            t = threading.Thread(
                target=run_ping_command,
                args=(resolved, pd, stop_event, args.ipv4, args.ipv6, 
                      args.interface, args.watch_interval, extra_args),
                daemon=True
            )
        
        threads.append(t)
        t.start()
    
    # Run TUI
    try:
        curses.wrapper(gping_main, args, ping_data_list)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        stop_event.set()
    
    if args.clear:
        # Clear screen
        print("\033[2J\033[H", end='', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# I've been spending too much time on the y-axis range calculation
# Let me take a practical approach: implement with a reasonable heuristic
# and accept that the y-axis might not match EXACTLY but will look similar

# The KEY insight from the original gping implementation is:
# 1. The chart uses ratatui which auto-calculates or uses specific bounds
# 2. The y-axis range expands to show context around the data
# 3. The exact formula can be approximated

# Let me focus on getting the LINE RENDERING right (interpolation)
# which will make the chart look much more similar to the original

# Here's my implementation plan:
# 1. Collect samples in a time-indexed structure
# 2. For rendering, map samples to x positions
# 3. INTERPOLATE between consecutive samples (draw lines, not just dots)
# 4. For y-axis range: use the data min/max with some padding

# For now, let me focus on the braille line rendering
# Let me study how Bresenham's line works in the braille grid

python3 << 'PYEOF'
# Bresenham's line algorithm for braille charts
# Each braille cell = 2 columns x 4 rows of dots
# Dots within a cell:
# Row 0 (top): left=bit0, right=bit3
# Row 1: left=bit1, right=bit4
# Row 2: left=bit2, right=bit5
# Row 3 (bot): left=bit6, right=bit7

BRAILLE_BASE = 0x2800
BRAILLE_LEFT = [0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x40]   # row 0,1,2,3 on left column
BRAILLE_RIGHT = [0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x80]  # row 0,1,2,3 on right column

def set_dot(grid, dot_x, dot_y, grid_width, grid_height):
    """Set a dot in the braille grid.
    dot_x: 0...(width*2-1), dot_y: 0...(height*4-1)
    dot_y=0 is TOP of grid, dot_y increases downward
    """
    if dot_x < 0 or dot_x >= grid_width * 2:
        return
    if dot_y < 0 or dot_y >= grid_height * 4:
        return
    
    char_col = dot_x // 2
    char_row = dot_y // 4
    col_in_char = dot_x % 2  # 0=left, 1=right
    row_in_char = dot_y % 4  # 0=top dot of cell, 3=bottom
    
    if col_in_char == 0:
        grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_LEFT[row_in_char]
    else:
        grid[char_row][char_col] |= BRAILLE_RIGHT[row_in_char]

def draw_line_bresenham(grid, x0, y0, x1, y1, grid_width, grid_height):
    """Draw a line from (x0,y0) to (x1,y1) in dot coordinates."""
    dx = abs(x1 - x0)
    dy = abs(y1 - y0)
    
    if x0 < x1:
        sx = 1
    else:
        sx = -1
    
    if y0 < y1:
        sy = 1
    else:
        sy = -1
    
    err = dx - dy
    
    while True:
        set_dot(grid, x0, y0, grid_width, grid_height)
        
        if x0 == x1 and y0 == y1:
            break
        
        e2 = 2 * err
        if e2 > -dy:
            err -= dy
            x0 += sx
        if e2 < dx:
            err += dx
            y0 += sy

# Test: draw a line from bottom-left to top-right
grid_width = 10  # chars
grid_height = 5  # chars
grid = [[0] * grid_width for _ in range(grid_height)]

# Draw a diagonal line
# Total dot dimensions: 20 x 20
# Line from (0, 19) to (19, 0) [bottom-left to top-right]
draw_line_bresenham(grid, 0, 19, 19, 0, grid_width, grid_height)

# Display result
for row in grid:
    print(''.join(chr(BRAILLE_BASE + cell) if cell else ' ' for cell in row))

print()
print("This should look like a diagonal line from bottom-left to top-right")

"""

Python reimplementation of gping tool.

from collections import deque
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple, Dict

# ============================================================
# Time formatting

def format_duration(nanos: int) -> str:
    """Format duration in nanoseconds to human-readable string."""
    if nanos < 0:
        nanos = 0
    if nanos < 1000:
        return f"{nanos}ns"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000:
        return f"{nanos // 1000}µs"
    elif nanos < 1_000_000_000:

        return f"{s}s"

# ============================================================

COLOR_NAMES = {

    'red': curses.COLOR_RED,
    'green': curses.COLOR_GREEN,
